evidence: Plin. Ep. 9.36.4: post cēnam cōmoedia aut lyristēs
terms.comment: With a time or an event: post cēnam, post merīdiem, post diēs decem. A thing is not a point in time: for “after the film” or “after the train” Latin says what happened, with a clause (postquam) or a participle (quō factō, when that was done).

terms.gloss: a few days later, a few days after
terms.grammar: phrase: post as an adverb, with the measure of time in the ablative
evidence: Cic. Att. 5.20.3: interiit paucīs post diēbus
Cic. Sen. 19: novem annīs post meum cōnsulātum
terms.comment: So paulō post, a little later; multīs post annīs, many years later.

phrases.latin: cēnantī mihi, sī cum uxōre vel paucīs, liber legitur; post cēnam cōmoedia aut lyristēs; mox cum meīs ambulō
phrases.english: at dinner, if I am with my wife or a few friends, a book is read aloud; after dinner, a comedy or a lyre-player; then I take a walk with my household

phrases.latin: post sōlis ortum fulgidī sērum est cubīle spernere
phrases.english: once the bright sun is up, it is late to be leaving one’s bed

phrases.latin: Post diēs autem decem, appāruērunt vultūs eōrum meliōrēs, et corpulentiōrēs
phrases.english: after ten days their faces looked better and plumper

phrases.latin: nam cum in loca aliqua post tempus reversī sumus, nōn ipsa agnōscimus tantum, sed etiam, quae in hīs fēcerīmus, reminīscimur
phrases.english: when we go back to a place after some time, we not only recognise it, but remember what we did there

phrases.latin: commodum discesserās heri cum Trebātius vēnit, paulō post Curtius
phrases.english: you had only just left yesterday when Trebatius came, and a little later Curtius

phrases.latin: quae crēbrius inter sē pugnābunt, aspargī eās oportet aquā mulsā. quō factō nōn modo dēsistunt pugnā, sed etiam conferciunt sē lingentēs
phrases.english: bees that keep fighting should be sprinkled with honey-water; after that they not only stop fighting but huddle together, licking each other
